newsitem.title: USA: Iowa planting progresses, but cold slows growth.
newsitem.headline: Iowa planting progresses, but cold slows growth.

text.p: Planting progressed rapidly in Iowa during the week ended Sunday, but cool weather much of the week delayed crop emergence, the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service said.

Sub-freezing weather was reported early Thursday and early Friday over the northern half of the state. A rapid warmup occurred Friday, with Sioux City reporting a record low for the date of 33 degrees Fahrenheit that morning and a record high of 91 later that same day.
Moisture was needed to soften crusted soil in some areas.
Corn planting was 94 percent complete versus 86 a year ago and the 73 average. Corn emergence was at 20 percent versus 17 a year ago and the 32 average.
Soybeans were 53 percent planted versus 19 a year ago and the 35 average.
Oats were 92 percent emerged versus 89 a year ago and the 83 average. The crop was rated seven percent excellent, 56 good, 32 fair and five poor.
Winter wheat deteriorated slightly with 11 percent rated excellent, 56 good, 26 fair, six poor and one very poor.
Pastures developed slowly due to the cold weather and conditions deteriorated from the previous week. Pastures were rated eight percent excellent, 46 good, 34 fair, 11 poor and one very poor.
